combat2_operational_work.evidence: Source tracing proved the stale_equipment loop: the installed claim projects current equipment for every historical fighter, resolver fences every projected item, and commit correctly demands each fenced fighter generation remain present. The correction limits both projection and resolver derivation/fencing to fighters present at the frozen claim boundary. A fighter who dies or departs during resolution remains fenced; absent-source offscreen effects keep frozen magnitudes and attribution; historical participation and qualified rewards remain. Focused resolver, worker, dispatcher, migration and durability tests cover the corrected boundary. The generated Combat2 resolver mirror changes transitively for combat2-tick-once and combat2-dispatch-once. Nothing is installed, deployed, published or live-verified.

The first reconciliation projected only the RPC's authoritative moved/already_moved destination and Mik operator-reports that its published solo path reaches the destination without the former fixed wait. Follow-up source tracing proved the occasional false finalizing state and flicker were frontend races: GamePage and Combat2ClientSession owned separate departure sessions; recovery was presented as real pending movement; older character/party refreshes could overwrite newer acknowledged location; and stale party rows could briefly misroute a rapid leader follow-up. The correction establishes one lifecycle, separates fail-closed recovery from genuine pending/queued state, skips stale recovery after an acknowledged terminal destination, generation/revision-fences character and party reads, bridges only acknowledged party members until refresh, and shares one input guard across command, pointer/map and keyboard movement. Focused tests cover duplicate input, stale recovery/reads, immediate A-to-B-to-C, absent Realtime recovery, character/session switch, party routing and Combat2 transition ownership. No optimistic destination, browser location/MP write, SQL, heartbeat, scheduler or server movement behavior was added or changed. The latest frontend correction requires Mik's manual publication; coordinated party/multiplayer and bounded live race verification remain pending.

Mik reports after publication that minimap mouse movement is immediate and no longer reports errors, while keyboard movement still has noticeable delay. Earlier he also observed occasional Movement is being finalized presentation and location flicker, addressed by the prior source correction. The exact published frontend revision is unavailable and is not guessed. This operator evidence verifies the minimap-visible path only; it is not direct verification of the latest keyboard correction, coordinated party movement, multiplayer races or installed server concurrency.

The timer never delayed the first RPC; it silently discarded a prompt later deliberate press even after authoritative completion and coherent destination rendering. The correction removes the fixed timer and explicitly ignores native held-key repeat, while the shared departure lifecycle continues to own single-flight, pending/recovery, authoritative connection selection, uncertain retry UUID reuse, stale response/session fencing and solo/party routing. Focused tests prove immediate first submission with zero timer, latest acknowledged origin on the next deliberate press, held-repeat suppression, disabled pending suppression and input/dialog exclusions. No targeting, initiation, ability, stance, movement, heartbeat, backend or engine rule changed.

Root causes were client delivery and presentation boundaries, not evidence of a changed server cadence. Character rows had scoped Realtime but no connection-state diagnostics or bounded visible-tab fallback, so tab focus could appear to be required when Realtime delivery stalled. Combat2 visible history was encounter-keyed and could be replaced or cleared at release, while the on-device archive received the legacy local log instead of the merged authoritative presentation. The correction retains scoped Realtime as primary, adds a coalesced four-second visible fallback and recovery refreshes, fences stale user responses, refreshes resources when an active Combat2 session exits, retains a bounded 100-event character-scoped log across release/movement/new encounters, and archives that merged view. Authoritative out-of-combat HP/CP/MP settlement is installed and composed into the existing world scheduler: one four-second logical interval, globally locked singleton cursor, already_settled short-circuit, short catch-up capped at three intervals, at most one interval after longer downtime, cursor advanced without banking while the world sleeps, combat mode is closed or the dispatcher schedule is absent. Settlement and Combat2 dispatch failures are independently contained with sanitized SQLSTATE evidence and the aggregate result is ok only when both domains succeed. Exclusions: death or missing location, Test Arena node, queued or just-resolved solo departure, queued or just-resolved party departure membership, fresh respawn request, fresh fighter release, and active-encounter ownership (present fighter with a living engaged creature in that same encounter, or a live claim). Peaceful co-location, inert shells, absent fighters and ended encounters do not suppress settlement. Formulas use final effective attributes from valid equipped durable gear and gems: HP from effective CON plus gear HP, gear regen, milestone and Inn bonuses; CP from effective WIS plus milestone and Inn; MP from effective DEX plus Inn. Caps are enforced, an already higher value is never lowered, browser-local food contributes nothing, Combat2 CP regeneration and Inspire are untouched and the browser has no resource writer or settlement privilege. Live regeneration is not yet verified; no settlement, dispatcher, worker, movement, combat, party or arena call was made.

Every dispatch attempt then returned commit_transport_error with PostgreSQL-category SQLSTATE 42703 (undefined column) at the commit stage. node_tick_commit and both installed wrappers trap all errors and return internal_failure, so a 42703 surfacing as a transport failure originates outside the PL/pgSQL body (PostgREST/pooler request handling or post-return deferred work). Ability submission did not bypass anything: it changed proposal content, so the failure is proposal-content dependent rather than input driven. Deferred-trigger candidates were inspected and release_stances_on_death is excluded (it returns before planning any statement while hp > 0). ROOT CAUSE PROVEN 2026-09-23 (static catalog audit, no encounter touched): the missing column is character_inventory.status (equally node_ground_loot.status), referenced as NEW.status by the installed trigger function public.enforce_unique_holder_identity(), authored in migration 20260917133413_fc7e672e-18b4-4103-9e8a-40f493fa167f.sql line 99. Installed body matched repository source byte-for-byte, so this is an authored source defect and not installed drift. The function is attached to three tables of different shape (character_inventory, node_ground_loot, marketplace_listings) as DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED constraint triggers; only marketplace_listings has a status column. PL/pgSQL resolves record field references when it prepares the entire IF expression, so "TG_TABLE_NAME='marketplace_listings' AND NEW.status<>'active' AND ..." raises SQLSTATE 42703 (record "new" has no field "status") on EVERY write to the other two tables regardless of the TG_TABLE_NAME guard. Because the trigger is deferred it fires at COMMIT, after node_tick_commit has returned, so the error escapes both wrappers' EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS handlers and reaches the worker as an unclassifiable commit transport failure. Failing branch: any proposal whose commit writes character_inventory, i.e. any tick recording weapon durability wear; proposals with no inventory write were unaffected, which is why an ability cast appeared correlated with progress. Static tests did not catch it because they assert column existence and authored SQL text, never PL/pgSQL record-field resolution against the installed table shape; the new guard closes that gap. Semantics confirmed in one single-connection transaction using only ON COMMIT DROP temp objects and a pg_temp clone, rolled back: the old expression raised 42703 at SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE, the corrected expression passed. No gameplay table was read for mutation, no public function was replaced in the probe, and all protected fingerprints (character_inventory durability, node_encounter tick/claim/state_version/status, characters hp/cp/max_cp/mp/reserved_buffs, node_creature hp/alive, node_intent, node_pending_event, node_tick_log) are byte-identical before and after.
